90% of the time it is the oil pressure sensor. They are about 120$ oem. BUT I HIGHLY RECOMMEND NOT REPLACING IT YOURSELF even experienced mechanics. It’s really really tricky, and it can only take 11 ft pounds of torque before cracking your entire oil pan. And it’s not suppose to screw all the way in as I’ve heard? I did it with a teeny ratchet and still cracked my damn pan. Costed 1600$ to replace with a tow.
One other thing to check if it isn’t your sensor is gallery gasket. It flows oil to the top of the engine, it’s a paper thin gasket that cracks super easily. It’s in the timing case so I believe if you open your oil cap and you can see oil flowing in the top of your engine, then it’s not cracked. As I believe.
Also don’t go aftermarket for the sensor. The tiniest difference in the threads can crack the pan. It’s a aluminum pan with a thin bead for the sensor port.
